latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Anti-PR3 antibodies bind cytokine-primed neutrophils expressing surface PR3, triggering degranulation, ROS burst, NETosis, and endothelial injury. Core pathogenic engine of GPA.
Fibrinoid necrosis of arterioles, capillaries, and venules driven by activated neutrophils and ANCA. Final common pathway producing organ ischemia/hemorrhage.
Geographic necrotizing granulomas with multinucleated giant cells, characteristic of GPA. Produces sinonasal destruction, orbital pseudotumor, subglottic stenosis, lung nodules/cavities.
Focal segmental fibrinoid necrosis with crescent formation in glomeruli; minimal Ig deposition. Drives RPGN phenotype and ESRD risk.
Neutrophilic capillaritis disrupting alveolar-capillary membrane causing diffuse alveolar hemorrhage, hemoptysis, and hypoxemia.
Granulomatous and ischemic destruction of nasal septum, cartilage, and sinus mucosa producing crusting, epistaxis, septal perforation, saddle-nose deformity.
Retro-orbital granulomatous infiltrate causing proptosis, diplopia, optic nerve compression, and risk of vision loss; often contiguous with sinus disease.
Granulomatous inflammation and fibrotic remodeling of subglottic/tracheobronchial tree producing fixed airway narrowing, often persistent or relapsing independent of systemic activity.
Middle-ear effusion, granulomatous otitis media, mastoiditis, and sensorineural hearing loss from cochlear vasculitis.
Multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules, often cavitating, due to necrotizing granulomatous inflammation; may mimic infection or malignancy.
Ischemic injury of peripheral nerves due to small-vessel vasculitis of vasa nervorum, producing painful asymmetric mononeuropathies.
Small-vessel cutaneous vasculitis producing palpable purpura, ulcers, livedo, nodules.
Necrotizing scleritis, episcleritis, peripheral ulcerative keratitis driven by ocular small-vessel vasculitis with risk of globe perforation.
Glomerulosclerosis and interstitial fibrosis following crescentic GN; drives irreversible CKD/ESRD even after remission.
Cytokine-driven systemic features (fever, weight loss, fatigue, arthralgia) accompanying active vasculitis.

Aggregate immunosuppressive burden from glucocorticoids, cyclophosphamide, rituximab, and methotrexate predisposing to bacterial, fungal, viral, and opportunistic infection (including PJP, HBV reactivation).
Active GPA carries elevated VTE risk via endothelial activation, NETosis, and inflammation-driven hypercoagulability.

mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Activated neutrophils degranulate and form NETs at endothelial surfaces, producing fibrinoid necrosis of small vessels.
Persistent neutrophil/macrophage activation and PR3-driven autoimmunity organize necrotizing granulomas in airway tissues.
Glomerular capillary necrosis triggers crescent formation as parietal epithelial cells proliferate.
Alveolar capillary necrotizing vasculitis disrupts the alveolar–capillary membrane producing DAH.
Ischemic injury to vasa nervorum from small-vessel vasculitis.
Skin small-vessel vasculitis manifests as palpable purpura, nodules, ulcers.
Episcleral and scleral small-vessel necrotizing inflammation produces scleritis and PUK.
Granulomatous and ischemic mucosal necrosis erodes nasal cartilage and bone.
Contiguous spread of granulomatous inflammation from sinuses into orbit produces retro-orbital mass.
Subglottic granulomatous inflammation heals by fibrosis, narrowing the airway.
Eustachian tube/middle-ear granulomatous inflammation produces conductive and sensorineural hearing loss.
Necrotizing granulomas in lung parenchyma form bilateral nodules and cavitate.
Healed crescents leave segmental glomerulosclerosis and tubulointerstitial fibrosis driving CKD.
Active vasculitis releases TNF/IL-6/IL-1 driving fever, fatigue, weight loss, arthralgia.
Endothelial activation, NETosis, and systemic inflammation in active GPA produce hypercoagulable state.
Pathogenic mechanism reflected in serum PR3-ANCA titer; rises in flares and falls with treatment though imperfectly.
GPA is classically c-ANCA (cytoplasmic) on IIF, not p-ANCA; pattern probability biased to cytoplasmic.

Acute-phase fibrinogen and globulin elevation.

Cytokine-driven fatigue.

Inflammatory myalgia.

Anemia of chronic inflammation; additional drop if DAH or renal failure present.
Reactive thrombocytosis in active inflammation; helps distinguish from MAS/TTP.

Stridor and tachypnea with critical stenosis.

mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Cochlear vasculitis and facial nerve compression in mastoiditis.

mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Mass effect on cranial nerves and optic nerve.
Mononeuritis multiplex with painful asymmetric sensorimotor deficits.

Pulmonary, cardiac, serosal, anemia, or systemic inflammatory involvement can cause dyspnea.
Pulmonary or airway involvement can cause cough.

PR3-ANCA positivity is a major GPA serologic pattern; record positivity separately from assay-specific titer magnitude.

axes.display_name: Lack of clinical response to standard antibacterial therapy
axes.shape_free_text: Persistent fever, inflammation, or organ findings despite antibacterial therapy that should have covered ordinary bacterial infection.
Patient-reported or observed breathlessness from pulmonary, cardiac, mediastinal, anemia, or systemic inflammatory involvement.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Both reflect GFR; move together with renal function changes.
Both acute-phase reactants; CRP rises and falls faster.
DAH causes alveolar blood loss and hemoglobin drop.
Active sediment precedes/parallels rising creatinine in crescentic GN.
Rising creatinine directly indexes AKI severity.

axis_couplings.conditionality: imperfect — rising PR3-ANCA does not always precede flare, especially in granulomatous-only disease
axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: PR3-ANCA correlates with disease activity but is an imperfect biomarker of flare.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Active untreated infection demands concurrent antimicrobial coverage; pulse steroids still given if life-threatening vasculitis but with caution.
Severe organ-threatening involvement is the indication for pulse therapy.
RPGN is a classic indication for pulse methylprednisolone.

treatments.context_specific_role: Initial 3-day IV pulse (typically 0.5–1 g/day x 3) for organ-threatening severe GPA (DAH, RPGN, severe CNS/ocular disease) before transition to oral prednisone.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Steroid use during active uncontrolled infection worsens infectious outcomes.

side_effects.interpretation: Cumulative infection risk; rises with cumulative dose

treatments.context_specific_role: Oral prednisone (typically starting ~1 mg/kg/day; reduced-dose PEXIVAS regimen now standard), tapered over 4–6 months for induction; continued at low dose during maintenance per protocol.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: HBsAg+/anti-HBc+ patients require antiviral prophylaxis (e.g., entecavir/TDF) before rituximab.
Preferred over cyclophosphamide in patients of reproductive age.
Generally avoided in pregnancy except life-threatening disease; planning pregnancy favors alternative.

side_effects.interpretation: B-cell depletion increases infection (esp. respiratory, PJP, late hypogammaglobulinemia)
Late infection hazard from prolonged B-cell depletion

treatments.context_specific_role: Induction (375 mg/m²/week x 4 OR 1 g x 2) for new-onset or relapsing GPA; maintenance dosing every 4–6 months for 18–24+ months. Preferred for younger patients, relapsing disease, granulomatous disease where cyclophosphamide may be less effective.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Dose reduction needed; metabolite accumulation increases toxicity.
Reproductive-age patients; cumulative dose risk pushes toward rituximab.
Teratogenic; absolute contraindication in pregnancy.

side_effects.interpretation: Marrow suppression; titrate dose to ANC
Marked infection risk including PJP and herpes zoster
Hemorrhagic cystitis (acrolein); mesna prophylaxis required for IV

treatments.context_specific_role: Induction (IV pulse 15 mg/kg q2–3w x 3–6 doses, or daily oral 2 mg/kg) for severe organ-threatening GPA when rituximab unavailable, contraindicated, or patient cannot complete maintenance follow-up. Alternative to rituximab in PR3-AAV induction.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Compatible with pregnancy; maintenance option for women planning pregnancy.

failure_modes: less effective than rituximab for relapse prevention
treatments.context_specific_role: Maintenance (after cyclophosphamide induction) at 1.5–2 mg/kg/day; less effective than rituximab for sustained remission but useful when rituximab unavailable or in pregnancy planning.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Renal clearance; toxic accumulation in CKD.
Teratogenic; absolute contraindication.

treatments.context_specific_role: Limited (non-organ-threatening) GPA: induction (15–25 mg/week PO/SC) and maintenance. Not for renal/DAH/severe disease.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Teratogenic; absolute contraindication.

failure_modes: less effective than rituximab/azathioprine for relapse prevention
treatments.context_specific_role: Alternative maintenance agent when rituximab and azathioprine are unsuitable.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Some clinical benefit in severe DAH suggested by subgroup data, though PEXIVAS did not show overall mortality benefit.
PEXIVAS showed no significant reduction in death/ESRD; routine use in severe AAV no longer recommended for renal benefit alone, though may be considered case-by-case.

failure_modes: no clear mortality benefit in PEXIVAS
treatments.context_specific_role: Selective rescue therapy for life-threatening DAH or refractory disease; routine use for severe AAV no longer guideline-supported after PEXIVAS, but still considered case-by-case.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Hepatotoxicity reported; avoid in severe hepatic dysfunction.

failure_modes: still requires concomitant rituximab or cyclophosphamide
treatments.context_specific_role: Adjunct to rituximab or cyclophosphamide in active AAV (ADVOCATE trial); enables steroid-sparing induction. Not used as monotherapy.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Effective PJP prophylaxis in immunosuppressed AAV patients.

treatments.context_specific_role: PJP prophylaxis during induction immunosuppression; also reduces upper-airway relapse rate in localized GPA at higher dose (controversial efficacy).

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Risk of further AKI; monitor closely or hold during acute injury.

treatments.context_specific_role: Renoprotection and BP control after induction once AKI stabilized; reduces proteinuria and slows CKD progression.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Mechanical narrowing requires mechanical/local-injection treatment; systemic immunosuppression alone often insufficient for established subglottic stenosis.

treatments.context_specific_role: Endoscopic dilation +/- intralesional steroid (or mitomycin) for symptomatic subglottic stenosis; may need repeat procedures.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Active DAH precludes anticoagulation.

failure_modes: bleeding (especially with active DAH or recent renal biopsy)
treatments.context_specific_role: Treatment-dose anticoagulation for documented DVT/PE during/after active GPA, balancing against DAH/biopsy bleeding risk.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Required for hyperkalemia, fluid overload, severe acidosis, uremic complications.

treatments.context_specific_role: Dialysis bridge during severe AKI; ~40–60% of dialysis-dependent GPA patients regain enough renal function to discontinue.
Bone protection during prolonged glucocorticoid therapy.

peak_50_70.trajectory_modulation: Peak incidence in 5th–7th decades; older patients have higher infection-related mortality.

northern_european.trajectory_modulation: Higher prevalence in northern European populations; PR3-AAV more common.

east_asian.trajectory_modulation: Lower GPA incidence in East Asian populations; MPO-AAV proportionally higher.

chronic_carrier.trajectory_modulation: Associated with relapse risk; rationale for TMP-SMX maintenance in upper-airway disease.

exposed.trajectory_modulation: Occupational silica exposure increases AAV risk.

hydralazine_propylthiouracil_levamisole_.trajectory_modulation: Drug-induced AAV more often MPO-positive but PR3 patterns reported; resolves with drug withdrawal.

current_or_former_smoker.trajectory_modulation: Modestly increased risk; potential link to airway/pulmonary phenotype.

male.trajectory_modulation: Slight male predominance in GPA; broadly similar disease severity.

supportive_care: PJP prophylaxis (TMP-SMX) during induction immunosuppression
HBV/HCV/TB/HIV screening before immunosuppression; antiviral prophylaxis if HBsAg+ or anti-HBc+ and rituximab/cyclophosphamide planned
Vaccination optimization before B-cell depletion (pneumococcal, influenza, COVID-19, zoster, HBV) when feasible
Bone health: calcium, vitamin D, bisphosphonate or denosumab during prolonged glucocorticoids; baseline DEXA
Glycemic monitoring and management of steroid-induced hyperglycemia
Blood pressure control with ACEi/ARB once renal function stabilized; sodium restriction
Mesna with IV cyclophosphamide; strict hydration and bladder protection
Monitoring of CBC weekly during cyclophosphamide induction; dose adjust to ANC and renal function
Serial monitoring of PR3-ANCA, CRP, urinalysis, and serum creatinine to detect relapse
Otolaryngology and pulmonology co-management for sinonasal/airway disease; serial laryngoscopy for subglottic stenosis
Ophthalmology evaluation for ocular disease (scleritis, orbital pseudotumor)
Saline nasal irrigation, mupirocin to nares for chronic S. aureus carriage
Hearing assessment and audiology follow-up for otitis/SNHL
Physical and occupational therapy for mononeuritis multiplex deficits and post-illness deconditioning
Reproductive counseling and fertility preservation (sperm/egg banking) before cyclophosphamide; contraception during cytotoxic therapy
VTE awareness and prophylaxis during hospitalization; treat documented VTE
Patient education on relapse symptoms (epistaxis, hematuria, hemoptysis, new neurologic symptoms) for early presentation
Smoking cessation
Cardiovascular risk reduction (lipid management, BP, antiplatelet when indicated) given accelerated atherosclerosis risk
Nephrology referral for CKD staging and dialysis/transplant planning when applicable
Mental health support for chronic illness, body-image issues from saddle-nose deformity, treatment burden
Multidisciplinary follow-up (rheumatology + nephrology + ENT + pulmonology) for long-term care
